name: Fernley Park

location.about: A Kent town of about 110,000 on the river below the Downs: hop gardens and oast houses, paper mills and the barracks. A club that has won the Founders' Cup six times and the league only once - the best cup side in the South.

colours.story: Hop green and white - the green of the hop gardens, the white of the oast-house cowls. The club began in 1874 in a park given to the town by a paper-mill owner, and took its name from it.

rivals.why: three cup finals - 1909, 1986 and 2021 - and Fernley won every one
the big London club up the line; Fernley beat them in the 1979 Founders' Cup final and still sing about it

history.title: The park club
history.text: Founded in 1874 by hop farmers and paper-mill clerks in the park that gave the club its name. Beaten in the 1876 Founders' Cup final, winners in 1893 (against Oakhurst), beaten again in 1900 - and once lost 10-1 at Stonecross, in 1894.

history.title: Champions, once
history.text: Second in 1904 behind Northwick; beaten by Holloway in the 1907 Founders' Cup final, winners in 1909 (Kingsmere). Second Division champions in 1912 - and in 1928 champions of England, ahead of Millbrook: the only title, and the old men of the town talked about it for fifty years.

history.title: The cup kings of the South
history.text: Long years in the Second Division: champions of it in 1956 and 1976, promoted in 1970 and 1973 as runners-up; beaten in the first Charter Cup final, 1961. Then the Founders' Cup two years running: 1979 against Eastvale and 1980 against Whitcombe. Promoted again in 1981.

history.title: In and out
history.text: The Charter Cup in 1986 (Kingsmere again), the Founders' Cup final lost in 1993; Division 1 champions in 1998; the Charter Cup final lost in 2001, up through the play-offs in 2002 (against Coldharbour). Division 1 champions again in 2020.

history.title: Cup kings again
history.text: Back-to-back Founders' Cups, 1979-80 all over again: 2021 against Kingsmere and 2022 against Westmoor. Relegated soon after - and back up through the play-offs in 2026, against Saltmarsh.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1928 = 1927-28).

legends.name: Sir Henry Fernley-Croft
legends.note: Paper-mill owner who gave the town the park - and the club its name.

legends.name: Terry Rootes
legends.note: Two Founders' Cups, a Charter Cup and two promotions.

legends.name: Kai Ashdown
legends.note: Scored in both the 2021 and 2022 finals.

records.attendance: 41,377 v Eastvale Wanderers, Founders' Cup sixth round, 1979 (Oast Lane, before seating)

badge.about: An oast house and a hop bine; six hop cones round the edge for the six Founders' Cups. Motto 'Crescit Eundo' - it grows as it goes.
badge.design: A hop-green circle with a white ring. In the centre a white oast house with its pointed cowl, and a hop bine with green cones climbing a pole beside it. 'FERNLEY PARK' in green capitals around the white ring, '1874' at the bottom; six small green hop cones evenly spaced on the ring.

ground.name: Oast Lane

stands.name: Paper Mill Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts, six Founders' Cup replicas in the trophy room

stands.name: Oast End
stands.features: the home end - two restored oast houses stand right behind it

stands.name: Weald Stand
stands.features: a long single tier built with the 1979-80 cup money; hop gardens and the Downs behind it

stands.name: River End
stands.features: away fans; by the river and the old mill

ground.surroundings: white-cowled oast houses behind the home end, hop gardens and the green Downs beyond the east stand, an old paper mill on the river, the barracks on the hill
ground.atmosphere: warm and sunny on a good day; on a cup night, the loudest ground in Kent
